chapter: The Dallas nightclub and Jesse Stone's band
title: The Taliaferro name and Booker T. Washington's work with Indians
summary: Budd guesses how the Washington family acquired Indian-sounding names after reading a book on Washington.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I notice most of these Booker T. Washington family names have a lot of Indian things in them, Taliaferro, and --
That's true. Well, you know how that --
Do you happen to know how that came about?
Yes, I think I have a knowledge. I have a --
I have a knowledge of that. In fact, I was browsing in a book store --
Yeah, hold it. What did you say, you were browsing in a bookstore, and what happened?

Yes. I was in California at the time, and in Los Angeles, and I was browsing in a book store and I came across a little book for ten cents, and it was written by Booker T. Washington, and the fact it was a first edition, and I bought this book and naturally, being close to the family and everything, I thought I should read this book, and in reading this book I found that Booker T. Washington had done an awful lot educating the American Indians.
So you ask me about Taliaferro, which was a sort of a name --

Well, where did they get these names from? I'm going to make a guess, because like in this book it said that he started off by saying he never knew who his father was, but his mother he did know of, and I -- well I can say that -- well, his father was probably white, and his mother black, of course.
But then again, by him doing so much to educate the Indians and everything, they -- you know, and maybe probably
being a blood brother, they might have tagged that name onto him, that he accepted, because I'm just guessing at this, because I mean, you know, it doesn't take very much for you to change your name.
